when_to_use: radio-friendly smooth jazz where polished restraint makes one vocal-like lead melody feel inevitable, with clear verse-to-chorus lift and consonant R&B harmony, 82-98 BPM

defaults.feel: straight, ultra-precise 16ths, no swing, expression carried by lead phrasing not timing

signature_moves: smooth slash chord: Fmaj7/G or Dm7/G instead of a plain G7, creating lift without introducing roughness
pedal bass: Cmaj9 -> Dm7/C -> Fmaj7/C -> Cmaj9, letting harmony open above a stable emotional floor
stepwise bass descent: Cmaj9 -> G/B -> Am11 -> C/G -> Fmaj7, giving a polished phrase quiet forward motion
sub-V backdoor resolution: Bbmaj7/C -> Fmaj7/G -> Cmaj9, adding one sophisticated turn while preserving ease
cadence_options: pre-chorus lift into a smooth slash chord so the chorus downbeat feels prepared rather than forced
chorus hook resolves cleanly to tonic maj9, allowing the melody to sound complete without a raw dominant landing
avoid: plain dominant 7th where a 9sus4 or slash chord would preserve the style's polished continuity
altered or blues-heavy dissonance that makes the lead struggle against the harmony rather than sing through it

hook_archetypes.name: headline-melody
hook_archetypes.rhythm: a clear 2-4 bar phrase with deliberate rests, shaped so a listener can remember its breath pattern after one chorus
hook_archetypes.contour: scoop or bend into one target, hold it cleanly, and add controlled vibrato only at the tail like a vocalist finishing a word
hook_archetypes.first_appears: Chorus, in a higher register than the verse so the lift is heard before it is analyzed

hook_archetypes.name: afterglow-adlib
hook_archetypes.rhythm: loose vocal-style fragments around the tonic, each leaving space for a keyboard chop or band response
hook_archetypes.contour: short calls that echo the chorus hook without turning into scalar improvisation
hook_archetypes.first_appears: Outro, after the main hook is familiar enough to survive being partially omitted

verse.note_lengths: relaxed lower-register phrases with 1-2 bar rests, creating trust through restraint
verse.contour: gentle and singable, withholding the widest interval and highest target for the chorus
verse.placement: on the grid; expression comes from tone and articulation, not drag

pre-chorus.note_lengths: slightly tighter phrases with less silence, signaling that the melody is gathering itself
pre-chorus.contour: rise gently with the slash-chord movement, avoiding a premature peak

chorus.note_lengths: the most continuous and memorable phrasing of the form, balanced by rests that preserve singability
chorus.contour: move into a higher register and make one held target the unmistakable center of the hook
chorus.placement: on the grid, confident, with vibrato only at note tails

solo.note_lengths: structured, vocal-like phrases that could plausibly become a second melody; avoid dense technical runs
solo.contour: remain near hook intervals and shapes, expanding expression rather than harmonic complexity

drum_skeleton.low_energy: soft cross-stick backbeat, velocity-shaped straight 16th hats, and steady shaker create polish without drawing focus from the lead
drum_skeleton.mid_energy: add light R&B kick syncopation and widen hat dynamics so the groove feels more open before the chorus
drum_skeleton.high_energy: switch to a layered full snare at the chorus and support harmonic thickening, while keeping the grid straight and the surface controlled

arrangement_defaults.layout_rules: begin with a polished but incomplete frame: guitar or e-piano, soft pad, and minimal drums. Verse lead enters low and unhurried so the chorus still has somewhere to go. Pre-chorus harmony should begin lifting before the arrangement fully opens. At the chorus, raise the lead register, deepen the snare, and widen the pad together so the form feels inevitable rather than merely louder. Keep the solo melodic enough to sound like another chorus thought. In the outro, let ad-libs circle the known hook while the arrangement gradually recedes.

anti_boredom_rules: the melody must preserve 1-2 bar spaces between major statements; constant filling removes the vocal illusion
the chorus must lift through register, snare character, harmony, and support layers rather than simple duplication of the verse
use a smooth slash chord at least once per form pass and let it prepare a melodic or sectional arrival
the solo must remain singable and hook-adjacent, offering a new emotional angle rather than technical proof
the drum grid remains straight at every energy level; all expressive contrast must come from density, timbre, harmony, and phrasing

bass_behavior.role: legato supporting counterline under a vocal-style lead
bass_behavior.rhythmic_relationship: lands precisely with kick while using stepwise connective motion
bass_behavior.density: medium and continuous without becoming a riff focus
bass_behavior.articulation: smooth fretless-style sustain and controlled slides

groove_intent.kick: light syncopation supporting slash-chord bass motion
groove_intent.snare: cross-stick in verses, layered full snare in choruses
groove_intent.ensemble_relationship: rhythm section remains precise while lead carries expression through bends and vibrato

distinguishing_traits: lead melody and timbral chorus lift are primary
consonant slash-chord harmony over a polished precise pocket
